name: Nazi racial theories
summary: The racial worldview of the Nazi movement and state: humanity divided into biologically fixed races of unequal worth, with a Nordic or Aryan master race at the top, Jews cast as a parasitic counter-race, Slavs and others as inferior, and history as a struggle between races. It held that racial purity had to be protected by eugenic, marriage and citizenship law and that the Aryan race needed living space in the East.
scope: Nazi racial theories as the defining sources present them: the racial doctrine of Hitler and the Nazi movement and state, 1920-1945, including its Nordic or Aryan master-race idea, racial antisemitism, race-mixing and racial-purity doctrine, racial hygiene and genealogical proof of descent, and the racial-struggle and Lebensraum thinking tied to it (USHMM's 'Nazi Racism' entry; Bendersky on a 'Nazi racial ideology'; Chapoutot on 'Nazi racial theories'). Its texts are Hitler's Mein Kampf, Zweites Buch and speeches, and the race-science of Günther, Rosenberg and Darré that the scholarship ties to the movement. It leaves out Nazism's other tenets (leader principle, economy, one-party rule: Nazism has its own entry), the pre-Nazi Aryan-race theory of Gobineau and Chamberlain, wider eugenics and scientific racism outside Germany, and neo-Nazism after 1945.
